problem:
Consider the following matrices:

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}7 & -8 \\ 4 & -5\end{aligned}],\,D=[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}],\,P=[\begin{aligned}∗ & 1 \\ ∗ & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

Given that $D={P}^{-1}AP,$   find the first column of the matrix $P.$

feedback.problem:
Consider the following matrices:

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}10 & -12 \\ 8 & -10\end{aligned}],\,D=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 0 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}],\,P=[\begin{aligned}-1 & ∗ \\ -1 & ∗\end{aligned}]
$$

Given that $A=PD{P}^{-1},$ find the second column of the matrix $P.$
feedback.worked_solution:
From the diagonal matrix $D=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 0 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}]$, we deduce that the eigenvalues of the matrix $A$ are ${\lambda }_{1}=-2$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=2.$

So, the second column of $P$ corresponds to the eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{2}=2.$ 

Now, we simply need to find an eigenvector that corresponds to ${\lambda }_{2}=2.$ Computing $A-2I,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}A-2I & =[\begin{aligned}10 & -12 \\ 8 & -10\end{aligned}]-2[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}8 & -12 \\ 8 & -12\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have a system of linear equations with the augmented matrix $M$ which we reduce to its row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}8 & -12 & 0 \\ 8 & -12 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}8 & -12 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix above has one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. From the first equation, we obtain ${x}_{1}=\frac{3}{2}{x}_{2}.$ Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{2}{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Therefore, setting ${x}_{2}=2,$ we get the eigenvector 

$$
{v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Finally, $P=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 3 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}].$
